title: Laser Engraver Accessories: Beds, Rotary Rollers, Air Assist
metaDescription: Which add-ons are worth buying for a diode laser engraver: laser beds from LONGER, Mecpow, Tyvok and SCULPFUN, a Creality rotary roller, a Mecpow air assist and a LONGER Y-axis extension, from $36.99.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: After you buy a laser engraver, the next purchases are usually small and specific: something to hold the workpiece, something to engrave round objects, something to keep cuts clean, and something to make the work area bigger. This guide covers seven catalog accessories in those four jobs, priced from $36.99 to $199. One rule applies to almost all of them: accessories are built for particular machines, so check compatibility in the title before you click buy.

items.label: Tyvok Honeycomb Laser Bed, 400x400 mm ($36.99)
items.value: Honeycomb bed, the cheapest here, for 400 mm-class machines

items.label: LONGER Laser Bed, 440x440x22 mm ($49.99)
items.value: Same 440x440x22 mm size as the Mecpow H44, from LONGER

items.label: SCULPFUN H5 Gen2 Laser Bed, 650x650 mm + Fan ($199)
items.value: Largest bed here, with a fan included

items.label: Creality Rotary Roller ($87.19)
items.value: For engraving round objects; the title says Creality lasers only

items.label: Mecpow Air Assist, 30 L/min ($44.13)
items.value: Air assist for the Mecpow X3S, X3 and X3 Pro

items.label: LONGER RAY5 Y-Axis Extension Kit, 375x825 mm ($69.99)
items.value: Extends the RAY5's work area along the Y axis to 375x825 mm

pros: A bed is the cheapest accessory that makes a visible difference: it holds the work off the table and helps smoke and heat escape
The Tyvok bed at $36.99 and the Mecpow H44 at $43.04 are both under $50
The SCULPFUN H5 Gen2 includes a fan and covers 650x650 mm, which suits large boards
A rotary roller opens a whole category of work, such as mugs and tumblers, that a flat bed cannot do
Air assist is the standard fix for scorched cut edges and flare-ups when cutting
The LONGER Y-axis kit turns a 400 mm machine into a long-format one at $69.99
cons: Compatibility is narrow: the Creality roller is for Creality lasers only, the Mecpow air assist for the X3 family, the Y-axis kit for the RAY5
The bed listings give only size, so check your machine's working area and frame before ordering
A 440x440 mm bed is not interchangeable with a 400x400 mm one, so match the size to your machine
Rotary rollers need setup and adjustment for each object, and results depend on the item's shape
The extension kit does not include the laser itself, and the listing does not say whether extra parts such as longer cables are needed, so confirm on the product page

items.question: Which accessory should I buy first?
items.answer: A bed. It is cheap and useful on every job. Air assist comes next if you cut, and a rotary roller if you want to engrave cylindrical items.

items.question: Can I use a LONGER bed on a Mecpow machine?
items.answer: The LONGER and Mecpow H44 beds share the same 440x440x22 mm size, but a bed also has to fit your machine's frame and sit within its working area. Check your machine's dimensions rather than assuming a match.

items.question: What does air assist do?
items.answer: It blows a stream of air over the cutting point. In general that clears smoke, reduces scorching and lowers the chance of flare-ups. The Mecpow accessory lists 30 L/min and is meant for the X3S, X3 and X3 Pro.

items.question: Do I need a rotary roller?
items.answer: Only if you plan to engrave round objects. For flat work such as wood, leather or acrylic you do not. The Creality roller works only with Creality lasers.

items.question: Is a bigger bed always better?
items.answer: No. The bed has to fit within your machine's working area. The SCULPFUN H5 Gen2 at 650x650 mm is for machines that can use that much area, so check before you buy.

items.question: What about safety?
items.answer: Accessories do not replace safety gear. Use laser-rated eye protection, ventilate the room and never leave a running laser unattended.

sections.content: Start with a bed that matches your machine, add air assist if you cut, and buy a rotary roller or extension kit only when a specific project needs it. Always check the model name in the title first, because most of these accessories fit only one brand or one series.
